Nikhil,

Your detailed introduction checked every box, and your profile matches exactly what we need: manual editing, the right tools, strong volume capacity, and a long-term mindset.

Before anyone moves into the full contract, we follow the same standard onboarding process regardless of experience. Every clipper begins with a first paid milestone of 6 clips so we can confirm alignment on style and brand standards.

Please complete these steps:
1\. Review the YouTube channel and Instagram account I will share with you
2\. Create 6 clips using that content
3\. Submit them by Thursday

Approval of your clips will trigger a video call, during which I’ll walk you through the full system: your daily task board, the payment dashboard that lets you track earnings daily, your assigned Instagram account, and everything else you need to hit the ground running.

The pay structure is:
— $7.50 CPM per 1,000 views
— $1200 maximum payout per clip
— Weekly and monthly performance bonuses

To be direct, the Lead Clipper path is very much on the table as you grow with us, especially given your volume capacity and the leadership mindset you already demonstrated in your message.

Confirm that you’re ready, and I’ll send the links now.

You’re hired, Nikhil—congratulations. This was a strong first set: you were the only clipper to finish before the deadline, and the quality supported that result. Your moment capturing was on point, and the font selection worked well.

Two small changes should guide your work going forward. One clip was too short, so remember that clips must remain within 20-120 seconds to deliver the complete message or goal. Also, the captions and letters did not use color; adding it will make them stand out more and should improve watch time.

These are not major problems, only points of polish. Overall, your first set was strong enough to secure the position.

Payment for these clips will arrive on Thursday. After that, you’ll be properly onboarded through a better guideline video explaining exactly how we create clips, the do’s and don’ts, and what is expected.

There is also a larger responsibility ahead: you will serve as the lead clipper for a pod of 12 clippers while continuing to produce your own clips. In addition, you’ll approve work from the other 11, keep the pod operating smoothly, and make sure everyone meets the standard. Before the role begins, I’ll walk you through how all of that will work.

Congratulations again—we’ll talk soon.

source_message.text:
Hi Nikhil,

I can see how much effort you put into this submission, and I appreciate that. Still, I need to be honest because I want you to succeed here.

The clips are not ready yet. If they went to review in their current state, they would not pass, and I do not want that outcome for you.

These are the specific changes required:

1\. **Remove every crazy effect** — all animations and flashy transitions need to go. Nothing should distract from the message; keep the editing clean and simple.
2\. **Use white text only** — there must be no colored letters, colored fonts, or text effects. The text should only be white.
3\. **Correct the fonts** — return to the brand guidelines and use the exact specified font instead of guessing.
4\. **Choose moments that teach something** — each clip must present a complete lesson or story from beginning to end, not merely a highlight or fragment. It needs to make sense independently and leave the viewer with something meaningful.

New videos have been added to the guidelines to demonstrate exactly what both a perfect clip and a bad clip look like. Review everything again—every video, example, and link—and do not skip any part.

Nikhil, you are halfway there. I’m offering you this chance because I believe you can do it, but your next submission has to be perfect. Work through the full guidelines and redo all 8 clips.

I’m rooting for you, so show me what you can do.

Darius

Brother,

Plan around the timing first: **DEADLINE: Thursday.** Every clip must reach me by Thursday morning—not Thursday night—because I have to review and approve all of them before they go live Friday. Anything I do not have by then does not get posted this week.

- Keep background music at low volume and never louder than Arden's voice
- Make each clip standalone so that even someone unfamiliar with Arden can watch it and understand it completely

Move fast. To strengthen each moment rather than merely fill space, use the B-roll only where it adds power to the message.

Submit your 12 clips as a Google Drive folder link, use your name for the folder title, and set the folder so anyone with the link can view it.

Because these are the first real clips going live, make every one perfect.

Darius
